---
title: "Engine changelog"
---

This article records changes to the browser engine in `inst/www/` (`mascot.js`, `mascot-motion.js`,
`mascot-host.js`, `mascot-parts.js`, `mascot-geometry.js`, `mascot-faces.js`, `mascot-player.js` and `mascot.css`),
newest first. User-facing R functions and arguments are
covered in `NEWS.md`.

# mascot (development version)

## 2026-10-23 — Character format version 1 settled for outside authors (#493)

**In brief:** The engine accepts what the R checker accepts and refuses what it refuses: `requires` is optional, a
top-level `$schema` and `x_` extension keys are accepted and never read, and a `note` is accepted wherever R accepts
one. An unknown capability is named in the error, and errors about kit effect settings point to the kit definition.

**Technical:**

* `mascot-parts.js`: an unknown name in `requires` gives "This file needs the capability ..." with the name. The
  band overrides (`lod`, its bands and their face flags) and a mood's face controls (and its reduced face) skip a
  `note` and keys that start with `x_`; the id walk does not descend into an extension key of a fixed-field object.
  `mascot.parts.capabilities` lists the supported and reserved capability names, for the parity test with the format
  policy.
* `mascot-motion.js`: a track object and the `motion`, `motion.change` and `motion.idle` objects accept a `note` and
  `x_` keys, and the motion settings never read them.
* `mascot-geometry.js`: a `ref` item accepts `x_` keys beside its overrides.
* `mascot-faces.js`: a clip on a kit effect item is refused at
  `$.face.kit_definition.effects.<id>.items[<n>].clip` (or `reduced_items`), and the `fade_at`, `amplitude` and `rate`
  checks report `$.face.kit_definition.effects.<id>.<setting>`, the paths the R checker uses.

## 2026-10-22 — A readable engine version, and comments that say what the code does (#464)

**In brief:** `window.mascot.version` gives the version of mascot that a page runs, in Shiny apps, `mascot_preview()`
and Quarto or R Markdown pages. A page that loads a second engine of another version keeps the first and says so in
the browser console, instead of ignoring the second without a word.

**Technical:**

* `mascot_dependency()` gives the `mascot.js` script tag a `data-mascot-version` attribute with the package version;
  `mascot.js` reads it into `window.mascot.version` (`null` when a page loads the file without it). Its load-twice
  guard warns once through `console.warn` when the second copy has another version.
* Comments in `mascot-host.js`, `mascot-player.js`, `mascot-parts.js`, `mascot-geometry.js` and `mascot.css` say what
  the code does now, without internal stage names or references to documents outside the package.
* `mascot-player.js` reads a gesture track's key values as `k.value` (normalised keys are always objects), and
  `mascot-host.js` drops a check for a missing description that an earlier line already makes.

## 2026-10-22 — The engine has one drawing path (#463)

**In brief:** The engine draws characters with `format_version` 1 only, the format of every built-in character and of
every character the R functions accept. The second drawing path, for the data shape of 0.0.2, could not be reached
from R and is removed: about 2,090 lines and 87 KB less JavaScript on every page. Nothing drawn through the R
functions changes.

**Technical:**

* `mascot-draw.js` is removed, and `mascot_dependency()` no longer lists it.
* `mascot.js` keeps `fps`, `readCharacter()` and `validColour()`; `draw()`, `validateCharacter()` and
  `checkCharacter()` are removed. Its load-twice guard now keys on `readCharacter`.
* `mascot-motion.js` keeps `mascot.motion.tracks`, `mascot.motion.shared` (with `swapTiming`),
  `mascot.motion.settings` and `mascot.motion.panels`; the player for the 0.0.2 shape, `mascot.motion.pose()`,
  `mascot.motion.frame()` and `mascot.motion.validate()` are removed. `mascot.mount()` always mounts with
  `mascot.runtime`.
* `mascot-player.js`: its header holds the player contract. `update({ character })` with a description that is not
  format version 1 fails with "update.character: expected a character with format_version 1".
* `mascot-host.js`: validation, the detail band check (`mascot.runtime.check()`), the gaze, the restore control and
  a swap without a mood always take the format-v1 route; the branches for the 0.0.2 shape are removed.

## 2026-10-21 — A page that reconnects into a new Shiny session starts the protocol again (#426)

**In brief:** After Shiny reconnects the browser into a new server session (`allowReconnect()` on Shiny Server or
Connect), mascots take `update_mascot()` calls again. Before, they kept their last state and ignored every update until
the page was reloaded.

**Technical:** `mascot-host.js` listens to `shiny:sessioninitialized` and, when the session id differs from the one it
knew, resets each live mascot's applied revision and its gesture and bubble watermarks to zero and publishes the
snapshot again as a new kind of start, `resume`, keeping the mount and its generation. The new session has issued no
numbers, so the old ones would have been rejected by both sides. A `template-needed` reply is answered with a `resume`
snapshot that carries the baseline. The page keeps what it shows until the new session sends a state (the server sends
nothing at resume unless the app has already called `update_mascot()` in the new session); that state then replaces the
old one, and the bubble written into the page by `mascot()` is not counted as a new bubble, so a dismissed bubble does not reopen. Within one
session nothing changes.

## 2026-10-20 — Removed the module namespace hint (#392)

`mascot-host.js` no longer has `suggestNamespace()`, the two-second development-mode hint for a missing `ns()`. It could
not be reached from Shiny, because R drops an update for an id that is not mounted, so no user ever saw it. The module
rule stays documented in `?mascot` and `?update_mascot`.

## 2026-10-19 — Palette kept on a swap when it names the incoming character's own colours (#358)

When a mascot swaps to a character whose own colours carry the selected palette id (its `native_palette`), the host
keeps that palette id and applies no palette colours, as it does for `original`.

## 2026-10-19 — Disabled menus (#350)

Menu click settings carry a `disabled` flag through validation and replacement.
The host reuses the action button's `aria-disabled` and activation guard: the
button stays focusable but opens nothing and sends no input. Disabling an open
menu closes it; replacing it with an enabled menu allows activation again.

## 2026-10-18 — Menu toggles no longer send action clicks (#349)

`mascot-host.js` sends `input$<id>_click` only for action buttons. Opening or closing a menu by pointer or keyboard
leaves the click count unchanged; choosing an item still sends `input$<id>_menu` with event priority.

## 2026-10-18 — Named palettes resolved in R (#336)

The host receives a palette id and its light and dark leader colours separately
from explicit overrides. It applies palette colours first, role overrides next,
and CSS last. R settles palette retention on character swaps and warns when the
incoming character lacks the id. Host patches outside Shiny also resolve a shared
palette against the incoming character, or drop it when unavailable, keeping explicit
overrides. Followers continue to use the character's rules.

## 2026-10-17 — Mascots show connection loss in Shiny (#70)

**In brief:** When Shiny loses its connection, every mounted mascot switches straight to its worried mood and announces
"Connection lost. Reload the page to continue." above the disconnect overlay. Updates received during the outage are
retained as the state to restore when Shiny reconnects.

**Technical:** `mascot-host.js` listens to Shiny `shiny:disconnected` and `shiny:connected` document events, keeps
the disconnect mood authoritative across updates and remounts, and restores the latest host state on reconnect.
`mascot.css` raises each mascot above the Shiny disconnect overlay.

## 2026-10-17 — Browser validation requires moving wave and nod gestures (#328)

The browser character validator now refuses a character without `wave` or `nod`, or with a gesture whose keyed values
never change. A wave needs a changing track on a non-root part; a nod can change any channel, including `root`.

## 2026-10-17 — Outlines sit under the fill, slim as in the drawings (#325)

**In brief:** Sela, Knurl and Neer looked heavier in the engine than in their drawings. The outline is now painted
under the shape's colour, as in the drawings: only its outer half shows, and its light edge sits outside the shape
instead of inside it. Their outline widths grow by half so the visible line keeps a clear weight (the package creator chose this
from three options). Tessa has no outlined parts and does not change.

**Technical:**

* `mascot.geometry` paints an item with `outline: true` in the order second outline, outline, fill, then the item's
  own `stroke`. Before, the fill came first and both outline strokes covered it.
* The same paint passes in a different order, so the drawing-work counts are unchanged.
* `sela.json` and `neer.json`: outline 3 to 4.5, second outline 5 to 6.5; `knurl.json`: 2.5 to 3.75 and 5 to 6.25 (its
  micro-band outline is unchanged).

## 2026-10-17 — The browser counts drawing work the way R does (#304)

**In brief:** Before a character is drawn, the browser works out the most drawing work it can ever need in each detail
band and refuses a band that is over its limits. It now counts everything R counts, with the same rules, so a
character that R accepts is accepted in the browser and the other way round.

**Technical:**

* `mascot.runtime.bound()` (`mascot-player.js`) counts all nine limits of the format: parts and one accessory per slot,
  the face kit (brows, eyes, eyelids, lashes, clips, mouth, blush, glow), kit effects, both declared and started by a
  gesture, the ground shadow, mood and reduced-motion item changes, clips and gradients.
* Glow is counted on the box a shape really covers (after `ref` and `transform` moves, rotation and scale), on the
  style a shared shape resolves to, and on the largest of an item's mood alternatives. R gained the last rule too
  (`R/character-work.R`): a mood that adds a stroke to a glowing item was counted too low on both sides.
* Scale ranges start from every part's resting scale, worn or not; `null` keys of `set` tracks are ignored. A clip
  whose target item is missing in a reachable variant throws `missing_reference` at `$.clip`, as in R.
* `mascot.geometry.bandBound()` and `checkBudget()` are removed: their only user was the Tessa bridge (#313), and
  they had drifted from the count in the runtime. `mascot.geometry.checkWork()` stays.
* Accessory part ids are built in one place, `mascot.parts.accessoryPartId()`.
* Tests compare the browser with R at 1e-12 for every reference character and Tessa in all three bands.

## 2026-10-17 — Accessory part ids can no longer collide (#312)

**In brief:** A worn accessory's parts get ids of the form `wear__<accessory>__<part>`, and authored ids may not
contain two underscores in a row. Before, the accessory `a_b` with part `c` and the accessory `a` with part `b_c`
both became `wear_a_b_c`.

**Technical:**

* `R/character-references.R` and `inst/www/mascot-parts.js` build the same expanded ids; the schema
  (`inst/format/character-v1.json`) and the browser check refuse `__` in authored ids at their path.
* Tessa's `lod.micro.hide` names her bow and clip parts with the new ids.

## 2026-10-17 — The provisional Tessa bridge is removed (#313)

**In brief:** Tessa has one drawing path now, the format-v1 engine. The temporary bridge that drew her old recipe
through the new modules, and the internal switch that turned it on, are gone. Nothing users see changes.

**Technical:**

* Removed `inst/www/mascot-tessa-adapter.js` and its tests, and every branch that read
  `mascot.internal.useCharacterAdapter` (`mascot.js`, `mascot-host.js`, `mascot-draw.js`, `mascot-motion.js`).
* The old recipe `inst/characters/tessa.json` left the package; the legacy tests read it from
  `tests/testthat/fixtures/characters/tessa.json`. The public recipe stays `inst/format/characters/tessa.json`.
* The visual tool (`tools/visual/`) draws the format-v1 path by default, with detail bands; `--adapter` is gone.
* Still here: the legacy drawing code (`mascot-draw.js`) and player (`mascot-motion.js`), used by tests of characters
  without `format_version: 1`.

## 2026-10-17 — Default character Tessa moves onto the format-v1 engine (#308)

**In brief:** The default character Tessa is now drawn and animated through the format-v1 character engine
(`inst/format/characters/tessa.json` played via `inst/www/mascot-player.js`) instead of the legacy drawing code.
`mascot(character = "tessa")`, `update_mascot()`, `mascot_preview()` and the mascot studio mount Tessa on the
format-v1 runtime, preserving all five moods, wiggle on mood change, gestures (nod, wave), anchors and accessories
(bow, clip), blink, sizes, and detail-band level-of-detail hiding at micro size. Public colour role names and theme
mappings continue to work without change.

**Technical:**

* `R/characters.R`: `character_json("tessa")` serves `inst/format/characters/tessa.json` (format version 1).
  The host detects format version 1 and dispatches Tessa to `mascot.runtime.mount()`.
* Public colour role mapping: all public colour role names (`body`, `rim`, `limb`, `sleeve`, `eyelid`, `blush`,
  `accessory`, and related roles) are preserved in `mascot_colour_roles("tessa")`. Internal role mappings ensure theme overrides
  map directly onto the format-v1 recipe.
* The restore button label for Tessa becomes "Restore Tessa, <shown status>" (e.g. "Restore Tessa, Resting, ready for the next piece."), matching
  format-v1 character conventions.
* `inst/www/mascot-player.js`: `ns.geometry.draw()` receives frame elapsed time and active colour overrides in options;
  `inst/www/mascot-host.js` safely guards controller availability during initial snapshot and mount.
* Legacy drawing code (`mascot-draw.js`), `inst/www/mascot-tessa-adapter.js` and the internal switch
  `mascot.internal.useCharacterAdapter` remain in place and kept intact until final look approval.

## 2026-10-16 — Format-v1 characters mount and run in the real host (#307)

**In brief:** A checked format-v1 character now mounts in the page host and runs end to end: it is drawn through the
format-v1 modules, moves along its own tracks, swaps with another character, restores after a remount, and shows its
own status, accessible label, gaze, theme and detail band. The default Tessa path is untouched and draws the same
pixels. Nothing public changes: custom characters are still internal, so no user sees this until the character API
lands.

**Technical:**

* `inst/www/mascot-player.js` (new): `mascot.runtime` compiles a checked character once (`compile()`, a weak cache that
  keeps failures too) and plays it. `mount()` returns the same controller the legacy player returns (`update`, `gesture`,
  `setMood`, `seek`, `redraw`, `setBand`, `pause`, `play`, `holdVisibility`, `destroy`, `current`, `onChange`). A frame is
  `tracks.frameAt()` (change, gesture, idle extra, breathing, blink, deadline settle, reduction), the mood's base channels
  (reduced ones under reduced motion), held look last, then `parts.frame()`, the ground shadow, the part layers, the face
  and each kit effect in the order the data declares (parts by layer, the face at its owner's layer plus 0.5, effects at
  their own layer). Colours are the character's roles, the user's overrides, then the mood's recolour with an explicit
  user colour winning, computed again only when the mood, reduction or overrides change. The channel table of a plain
  frame is one object per player; the face controls, the draw view and the shadow channels are reused. Validation of a
  whole patch comes before any state or pixel changes; a frame is resolved and checked before the canvas is cleared.
* Swaps keep the legacy timeline: the outgoing character waves (its own `wave` tracks laid over the captured channels)
  and fades out over thirty frames, the incoming one waves and fades in over thirty, composited once through a private
  canvas, with durations fitted to the incoming activity window. A new target mid-fade keeps the exit time that remains,
  asking for the exiting character again reverses directly, a mood change mid-swap commits without a wiggle and does not
  extend it, a gesture during a swap is dropped, and reduced motion or `swap: false` is instant. Without a mood in the
  patch the incoming mood follows the contract's chain (`mascot.parts.swapMood()`). The legacy speed limit on a very early
  reversal (`recoveryFrames()`) is not ported: the recovery lasts the entrance that remains. A format-v1 character cannot
  swap into a legacy one or back; `update()` rejects it before any change.
* Detail bands: `bound()` is the componentwise upper bound of the painted work of parts and their items per band: the main
  anatomy plus, for each exclusive accessory slot, the largest declared accessory (one compile per accessory, not a product
  over slots), blur by maximum; frozen and cached per character and band. `check()` throws `budget` at `$` before any
  painting, and a band that passed once is not checked again. As `mascot.geometry.bandBound()` does, it counts parts and
  items only: the face, the ground shadow and the effects are not counted here, so browser and R counts still differ there
  (#304).
* Gaze: held look is `face.look_x` and `face.look_y` only. `compile()` records whether the face can look (a kit with an
  elliptical pupil); a faceless character or a kit of arcs, paths and dots has no gaze channels, and the host sends none.
* `inst/www/mascot-host.js`: a format-v1 description is detected with `mascot.runtime.isFormat()`. Mood and gesture checks go
  through `mascot.runtime.validate()`; the gaze goes to `face.look_x`/`face.look_y`, flipped back by the shown mood's
  `root.flip`, and is cleared with the same channels; the band follows the canvas width for a format-v1 character with no
  switch (the legacy path still needs the internal adapter switch); a swap without a mood records the incoming mood by
  the fallback chain, so the host's mood matches the player's; the restore control is named with the shown status instead of
  a mood id and takes its colours from the brand leaders. `mascot.host.state()` also reports `band`. Status in mood mode, the
  accessible label, themes, bubbles, panels and the four public inputs already read the description generically and are
  unchanged.
* `inst/www/mascot-motion.js`: `mascot.mount()` hands a format-v1 character to `mascot.runtime.mount()` and every other
  character to the legacy player; `mascot.motion.shared` exports the guards both players use (`named`, `object`,
  `overrides`, `same`, `swapTiming`, `recoverPose`, the patch field names) so each rule has one copy; the legacy player
  rejects a format-v1 character in `update()` with a clear message. `inst/www/mascot.js`: `checkCharacter()` dispatches the
  same way.
* `R/mascot.R`: the dependency now ships `mascot-parts.js`, `mascot-geometry.js`, `mascot-faces.js` and `mascot-player.js`
  (144 KB uncompressed together, by `wc -c`) before the host. `R/preview.R`: `mascot_preview()` resolves its theme through the
  same boundary `mascot()` uses, so a character that is not built in no longer fails its theme check there.

## 2026-10-16 — R-settled Shiny state and mount generations (#305)

**In brief:** Shiny sends the latest complete accepted state for one mount generation. A connection ledger
preserves gesture consumption and bubble dismissal when an element is replaced. The canvas label follows
the status of the character and mood actually shown.

**Technical:** `mascot-host.js` checks complete versioned envelopes before installation, ignores stale
revisions and terminated generations, publishes mount and state snapshots with event priority on the existing input,
and restores open bubbles with their remaining lifetime. Duplicate live ids leave the first binding
authoritative. The unversioned patch path remains for browser-only/custom hosts. Optional envelope metadata
is ignored; the version 1 core state and snapshot shapes are checked. Unknown static UI tokens trigger a
one-time baseline exchange, allowing pages rendered before the server starts and cached pages to bind after a server restart or
cache eviction. R checks every baseline field, character content, payload limits and the content-derived
token before accepting it into session-owned storage; invalid baselines show a diagnostic. Dynamic tokens
remain session-owned. Checked character metadata and content keys use bounded immutable caches.
The public argument forms remain unchanged; target-specific forms are internal until their API unit lands.

## 2026-10-16 — Reserved capabilities rejected in R and the browser engine (#306)

**In brief:** Every capability and field the format reserves for later (`extends`, `connector`, `ring_pulse`, `follow`,
`particles`, `morph`, `blend`, `inputs`, `fit`, `wardrobe` and `vividness`) is rejected with the stable code `capability`
and the message "not supported by this version of mascot". Nothing is ignored or partly run. No reserved feature runs,
and no shipped character uses one.

**Technical:**

* `inst/www/mascot-parts.js`: `compile()` first rejects a name in `requires` that is not one of the eight supported
  capabilities, at `$.requires[n]` (R does the same). A reserved name is then rejected only as a key of a fixed-field
  object, at its own path (for example `$.parts[0].follow`, `$.parts[0].items[0].blend`, `$.accessories.badge.fit` or
  `$.palettes.sea_glass.vividness`). Position decides, not the name of the parent key. The fixed objects follow
  `inst/format/character-v1.json`: an `object` with `fields` is closed, as R treats it. Map keys (ids, colour and
  recolour roles, style ids, track targets) and the free numeric tree `face.tune` are never checked, so a colour role
  called `follow` and a kit eye style called `follow` compile. Before this change these keys were ignored.
* Order: R reports the first problem in document order. The engine checks the top-level object first, then each
  object as it reads it (`lod`, parts, anchors, face, moods), then the objects it does not read (palettes, paints,
  gestures, unworn accessories and the rest) after its structural checks. So the two can differ when a reserved key
  comes before a structural error in the document: the engine reports a top-level reserved key first, where R reports
  the structural error if it comes first. Both results are pinned in the tests (`test-character-check.R` and
  `test-engine-parts.R`).
* `R/character-format.R`: a reserved name in `requires` now gives the version message; the R checker already rejected
  each reserved field with code `capability` at its path.
* Fixtures: ten new invalid recipes in `tests/testthat/fixtures/format/invalid/`, one per reserved name still missing
  (`particles` keeps its existing fixture). Each differs from its base recipe only by the reserved entry and is listed in
  `diagnostic-expected.json`.

## 2026-10-16 — Internal detail bands, band policy and atomic band changes (#303)

**In brief:** The internal Tessa adapter can draw in three detail bands (full, small and micro), chosen from the
canvas's untransformed CSS width. Each band applies its own overrides and refuses work over its budget before anything
is painted. A band change on resize is atomic: a refused band keeps the old one and is reported once, and a change
redraws without replaying motion. Nothing changes by default; all of this sits behind the internal adapter switch.
Full parity between the browser and R work counts follows in #304.

**Technical:**

* `inst/www/mascot-parts.js`: `bandFor(width)` classifies the exact CSS width (micro below 48, small from 48 to
  127.999, full from 128) and rejects a non-finite or negative width. `compile()` checks band overrides first:
  `lod.full` and any other name other than `small` or `micro` reject with `unknown_key` at the authored path (R does the
  same); an unknown key, a `face` flag other than `scale`, `lashes`, `brows` or `iris`, or a non-boolean `glow` are
  rejected at their paths; `lod.micro.glow: true` is rejected with code `budget` at root path `$`, and the message names
  the band, the key and the fix. Part `lod` lists must name bands.
* `inst/www/mascot-geometry.js`: `bandBound(compiled, band)` gives an upper bound on the painted items, paint passes,
  path numbers, glow emitters and blur of the geometry of the parts (including `lod.hide`, part and item `lod`, and
  glow passes). It keeps the largest candidate of each part's variants, is frozen and cached per compiled character and
  band.
  Worn accessories are counted as parts. It does not yet count the face, the ground shadow, the effects, mood item
  paints or the reduced-motion items that R counts, nor clip applications, gradient uses or the glow area ratio. `checkBudget(compiled, band)` throws `budget` at `$` naming the
  metric and limit. `bandCaps` mirrors the counted metrics of `inst/format/policy-v1.json`.
* `inst/www/mascot-tessa-adapter.js`: `bound(character, band)` is the componentwise maximum of `bandBound()` over every
  scene the character can reach: the feet tucked or not, times every selection of its declared accessories with at most
  one per slot (a selection the drawing refuses is skipped). It is frozen and cached per character and band. `check()`
  throws `budget` at `$` when that bound is over the band's caps, without painting. `draw()` checks first, then builds
  and paints, so a refused band never paints; the carried `lod` and the band reach `frame()`.
* `inst/www/mascot.js`: `ns.draw` passes the band to the adapter branch only; `ns.checkCharacter(character, band)` runs
  the adapter's per-character check without painting (a no-op with the switch off).
* `inst/www/mascot-motion.js`: `mount()` accepts `band`. `drawFrame()` checks the visible character before it clears the
  canvas, so a refused frame keeps its pixels. `controller.setBand(name)` checks the visible character first and throws
  with the old band, canvas pixels and state unchanged when the new band is over budget. It returns true when it drew and
  false when the band was already set. `update()` checks an incoming character before any state changes.
* `inst/www/mascot-host.js`: `mount()` checks the band the canvas measures and mounts at it, so a small mascot never
  draws a full-band frame first; a band over budget mounts at `full` with one warning. A width that is not laid out (not
  a pixel width, or a hidden container) mounts at `full` and decides the band on the first real measure. `measure()` calls
  `setBand()` only when the band changes; a refused band keeps the old one, measuring goes on, the refusal is reported
  once per band through `console.warn`, and nothing is thrown out of `measure()`. The canvas is redrawn once after a
  resize: by `setBand()` when it drew, otherwise by `redraw()`. All of this runs only when
  `mascot.internal.useCharacterAdapter` is true.
* `R/character-work.R`: `character_format_work()` refuses `lod.micro.glow: true` with code `budget` at root path `$`, the
  same diagnostic as the browser, so the R checker rejects it.

## 2026-10-16 — Internal format-v1 mood channels, recolour, switches and kit effects (#302)

**In brief:** The parts and motion modules can now resolve format-v1 mood channel hierarchies, acyclic recolour
role redirection, item overrides, variant anchors, declarative threshold switches, kit effects progress and
swap mood fallback chains. Nothing changes by default; all character changes operate behind internal compile
and adapter switches.

**Technical:**

* `inst/www/mascot-parts.js`: channel vocabulary validation against known rig target channels (`root.*`, `face.*`,
  `effects.*`, and part transforms); merge resolution in contract order (part resting defaults -> named pose ->
  mood channels -> reduced channels); compile-time validation requiring core moods (`idle`, `thinking`, `happy`,
  `worried`, `celebrating`), metadata schema checks, and fallback chain traversal ending at core moods (`swapMood()`); acyclic
  colour role redirection (`recolour`, `reduced.recolour`) resolving before paints and gradients with explicit user
  overrides taking priority and cycle detection rejecting with `invalid_colour`; item overrides (`fill`, `stroke`,
  `alpha`) applied per part item with undeclared target/colour validation; declarative threshold switches
  (`switch: { channel, above, variant }`) evaluating strictly above the threshold; variant anchors recomputed
  when owning part variant changes; numerical kit effects progress helpers (`sweatProgress()`, `sparklePulse()`)
  with reduced motion handling.
* `inst/www/mascot-geometry.js`: `draw()` honours dynamic mood item overrides (`state.item_overrides`,
  `options.items`) for item fill, stroke and alpha.
* `inst/www/mascot-motion.js`: carry-overs resolved for `pose()` bridge passing `reduced: Boolean(state.reduced)`
  and `idle: state.idle !== false`; deterministic seeded idle extra start time scheduling when `state.extraAt` is
  omitted using the window-proportional seeded hash rule, with suppression when `state.extraAt` is explicitly `null`.

## 2026-10-16 — Internal part glow, blur units and drawing-work accounting (#300)

**In brief:** Saved-format characters can give one item of a part a soft glow in a palette colour. Glow is drawn on a
small surface sized to the item, so it costs little, and it fades with the mascot. Nothing changes by default; the
provisional adapter uses it behind its internal switch.

**Technical:**

* `inst/www/mascot-geometry.js`: `glowPass()` emits one blurred pass per fill or stroke of the named emitter item on
  a backing-pixel scratch surface sized exactly for that pass (output never depends on an earlier pass), crops the
  distant shadow band and multiplies the caller's alpha. `backingBlur()` converts design units to backing pixels
  (`blur * cssWidth / 300 * dpr`); `scratchBounds()` inflates the transformed item box by three blur radii. Glow is
  off in the micro band and at alpha 0; emission-only items are drawn and counted.
* `inst/www/mascot-geometry.js`: `draw()` reports active parts, glow emitters and blur design units beside the
  existing counts; `combineCounts()` sums additive counts, keeps the largest blur and counts each part once across
  draw calls. The part lookup is built once per compiled character; compiled data is never changed while drawing.
* `inst/www/mascot-faces.js` and `inst/www/mascot-tessa-adapter.js`: faces use the shared glow pass and both use the
  shared count combiner.
* `R/character-work.R`: a glow paints a solid colour, so it adds no gradient use; a fill-and-stroke emitter counts
  two blurred passes, as the contract says (fill and stroke never merge).

## 2026-10-16 — Internal format-v1 tracks, needs and fallback, interruption and deadlines (#299)

**In brief:** The motion module can now evaluate saved-format gestures (tracks, fallback gestures, the five easing curves,
interruption, reduced motion and the five-second deadline) as pure functions. Nothing changes by default;
the provisional Tessa adapter can use it behind its internal switch.

**Technical:**

* `inst/www/mascot-motion.js`: added `mascot.motion.tracks`: `normalise()`/`sample()` for `[[at, value, ease?], ...]`
  and `{ mode, keys }` tracks (add and set modes, null as the mood base, discrete values that switch at keys,
  `linear`/`ease_in`/`ease_out`/`ease_in_out`/`step`, exact rest at the end); `compile()` for needs and fallback
  traversal (missing, cyclic and unplayable chains error with `{ code, path }`), target-part checks and the 1 to 150
  frame budget; `settings()` for the motion defaults and limits; `fit()` for late effects; `frameAt()` for one
  frame-by-frame result with interruption, reduction, absolute deadline settlement, multiplicative breathing, blink
  skipping and separate effect instances; `drawn()` for the frames a window draws.
* `inst/www/mascot-motion.js`: `pose()` replaces the legacy change and gesture layers with these tracks only when
  `mascot.internal.useCharacterAdapter` is true and `mascot.internal.tracks[id]` is registered. Idle stays legacy.
  Differences from the legacy gestures on Tessa: the nod adds its offsets to the mood (celebrating lifts
  from its own 10, not from an absolute -3); a hop follows `height * sin(pi * u)` instead of a parabola. Everything
  else matched to 1e-9 over every mood, gesture and half-frame.
* Room to grow: unknown gesture, channel, easing or effect names are errors, new optional fields keep defaults,
  and morph, blend and particle behaviour stay reserved. The idle `extra` start time is not defined by the
  format yet, so the scheduler accepts `state.extraAt` from the host rather than inventing one.

## 2026-10-16 — Filter page mutations, batch layout reads and pause off-screen mascots (#295)

**In brief:** Mascots ignore unrelated page changes unless an inline bubble needs refitting. Relevant
layout checks batch into one animation frame, and animating mascots pause drawing while scrolled outside
the viewport.

**Technical:**

* `inst/www/mascot-host.js`: filtered `MutationObserver` records (`relevantMutation()`) so attribute and
  child-list mutations outside a mascot's ancestor chain, `.mascot-source` anchor, `<head>` styles or
  `#shiny-notification-panel` do no work; coalesced `refreshPage()` and theme-mode mutations through
  `schedulePageRefresh()` into at most one `requestAnimationFrame` per burst. Compare each attribute
  transition and ignore changes confined to private host style properties, preserving application theme
  changes and source removals in the same task. While an inline bubble shows, also watch sibling layout
  changes so the message remains inside the viewport. Expose `measures` and `offscreen` in
  `mascot.host.state(el)`.
* `inst/www/mascot-host.js`: added a shared, reference-counted `IntersectionObserver` (`watchViewport()`)
  that calls `controller.holdVisibility()` when a mascot leaves or re-enters the viewport.
  `inst/www/mascot-motion.js` keeps that hold independent of user pause and activity: returning does
  not draw, renew the five-second window or override another pause. Moving players continue from
  their saved frame without clock-based catch-up. The observer disconnects on the last unmount.
* Browser regressions cover coincident application and host writes, sibling layout changes, active scrolling,
  and rested or explicitly paused players returning to view; budgets count work rather than elapsed time.

## 2026-10-16 — Internal generic faces and default glow alpha (`a35da74`, `df2895c`)

**In brief:** Internal character-format previews can draw generic face kits, and omitted glow alpha
uses full opacity.

**Technical:**

* `inst/www/mascot-faces.js`: added internal face-kit painters; `mascot-draw.js` resolves and draws
  generic faces on character-format anchors (`a35da74`).
* `inst/www/mascot-faces.js`: defaults omitted glow alpha to one (`df2895c`).

## 2026-10-16 — Cache compiled Tessa adapter scenes and shadows (`d13f301`)

**In brief:** Tessa's `format_version: 1` bridge reuses its compiled part tree and ground shadow across
frames instead of rebuilding and cloning the character on every frame.

**Technical:**

* `inst/www/mascot-tessa-adapter.js`: added `WeakMap` caches `scenes` (keyed by character object, then
  `JSON.stringify([tucked, !!character.arms, names])`) and `shadows` (keyed by character object) so
  `ns.parts.compile()` runs once per worn-accessory and foot-tuck combination rather than on every
  `draw()` call.
* `inst/www/mascot-tessa-adapter.js`: kept `ns.drawing.accessories(character, pose)` before the cache
  lookup so duplicate accessory slots still fail immediately on cached scenes; bound per-call colour
  overrides and alpha roles after cache retrieval via `bindings`.
* `inst/www/mascot-tessa-adapter.js`: moved arm rotation into `arm_left.rotate` and
  `arm_right.rotate` channels; the earlier adapter rebuilt parts with per-pose arm angles.

## 2026-10-16 — Respect part layer overrides and guard known paint layers (`9c87017`)

**In brief:** The Tessa adapter honours custom layer overrides on body, feet, arms and accessories and
rejects unknown part layers rather than silently skipping parts that sit outside the layers it interleaves
with the face and effects.

**Technical:**

* `inst/www/mascot-tessa-adapter.js`: forwarded `character.body?.layer ?? 1`, `feet.layer ?? 0`,
  `arms.layer ?? 4` and `item.layer ?? 3` when building the adapter's part hierarchy, and guarded
  `state.parts` layers in `scene()` so any part layer outside `{0, 1, 3, 4}` throws
  `mascot: unsupported part layer <n> for part '<id>'; must be in {0, 1, 3, 4}`.
* `inst/www/mascot-tessa-adapter.js`: ensured `draw()` calls `scene()` before touching the canvas so
  missing modules or unsupported characters leave caller canvas state and pixels untouched.

## 2026-10-15 — Expand the internal Tessa adapter (`66ed30f`, `9b850ce`)

**In brief:** Added an internal opt-in bridge (`mascot-tessa-adapter.js`) that draws Tessa's body, feet,
arms, shadow and accessories through the `format_version: 1` parts and geometry modules while mounting the
existing face and effect painters on resolved part matrices.

**Technical:**

* `inst/www/mascot-tessa-adapter.js`: implemented `window.mascot.tessaAdapter` (`{ scene, draw }`, frozen)
  translating legacy Tessa descriptions (`body`, `feet`, `arms`, `anchors`, `accessories`, `shadow`) into
  `format_version: 1` part hierarchies and channel maps (`root.lift`, `root.rotate`, `root.scale_x`,
  `root.scale_y`, `root.flip`); arm rotation becomes channel-driven in `d13f301`.
* `inst/www/mascot-tessa-adapter.js`: preserved legacy fill-only item `alpha` semantics (where
  `format_version: 1` item `alpha` multiplies both fill and stroke) by synthesising `RGBA` colour roles per
  alpha-bearing item.
* `inst/www/mascot-draw.js`: added `drawFace(..., placed = false)` and an internal opt-in branch
  (`window.mascot.internal?.useCharacterAdapter === true`) in `character()` that delegates to
  `ns.tessaAdapter.draw(...)` and mounts `drawFace`, `drawSparkle` and `drawSweat` onto the resolved `face`
  anchor and `torso` part transforms.

## 2026-10-14 to 2026-10-15 — Character format v1 parts and geometry modules (`651ca64`, `346e9bf`)

**In brief:** Added the two core runtime modules for character format v1: hierarchical `2D` part transforms
(`mascot-parts.js`) and `Path2D` shape compilation, clipping, outlines and gradients
(`mascot-geometry.js`).

**Technical:**

* `inst/www/mascot-parts.js`: added `window.mascot.parts`
  (`{ identity, own, multiply, point, root, child, compile, frame }`, frozen).
  * Enforces `format_version === 1`, reserved part identifiers (`root`, `face`, `effects`), unique
    `snake_case` identifiers, single accessory per slot, acyclic part and anchor dependency ordering, and
    deep-frozen compiled scenes via `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(character))`.
  * Computes per-frame `2D` affine matrices (`[a, b, c, d, e, f]`), `keep_upright` and `no_flip`
    orientation filtering, channel-driven variant switches (`part.switch`), detail-band (`full`, `small`,
    `micro`) hiding and variant overrides, and layer and declaration sorting.
  * Uses `Object.hasOwn` (`own()`) for all data-named lookups (`parts`, `anchors`, `accessories`,
    `variants`) to prevent `Object.prototype` pollution (`346e9bf`).
* `inst/www/mascot-geometry.js`: added `window.mascot.geometry`
  (`{ commands, compile, paint, draw }`, frozen).
  * Compiles `path` (absolute `M/L/Q/C/Z`), `circle`, `arc`, `ellipse`, `rect`, `round_rect`, `polyline`,
    `polygon`, `hexagon` and `ref` shapes into cached `Path2D` instances (`prepared` `WeakMap` keyed by
    compiled scene and `${partId}.${variant}[${index}]`).
  * Supports linear and radial canvas gradients (`2..6` ordered colour stops with role-resolved alpha),
    dual cartoon outlines (`outline` and `outline.second` with per-band overrides), detail strokes, and
    cross-part `Path2D` clipping (`style.clip`) with singular-matrix guards (`|det| < 1e-12`).
  * Returns per-draw work counters (`{ painted_items, paint_passes, path_numbers, clip_applications, gradient_uses }`)
    for budget verification.

## 2026-10-13 — Redraw sharp after restoring from minimised (`ace06f5`, #275, #276)

**In brief:** Restoring a minimised floating mascot immediately re-measures the canvas and redraws at full
device-pixel resolution, both before and after the restore animation.

**Technical:**

* Uses the existing `controller.redraw()` (introduced in `ea35c6f`) to repeat `drawFrame()` at the
  current frame without resetting `activeAt`, advancing time, or scheduling `requestAnimationFrame`.
* `inst/www/mascot-host.js`: called `measure(record)` and `record.controller.redraw()` immediately when
  restoring from minimised and again in the restore Web Animations `onfinish` and `oncancel` clean-up, and
  whenever `measure()` changes `canvas.width` or `canvas.height`.

## 2026-10-13 — Nested Shiny modules, `golem` and `rhino` support (`44e0e81`, #133, #273)

**In brief:** Added examples for nested `Shiny` modules, delayed `renderUI` outputs and re-rendered
containers; the host now reports minimise and restore actions back to the server.

**Technical:**

* `inst/www/mascot-host.js`: emitted `input$<id>_minimised` (`priority: 'event'`) when minimising or
  restoring.

## 2026-10-12 — Public CSS styling hooks and private `--_mascot-*` internals (`5157974`, #260, #270)

**In brief:** Separated public `CSS` custom properties (`--mascot-panel-*`, `--mascot-restore-*`,
`--mascot-z-index`) from internal layout variables (`--_mascot-*`) so user style sheets always win over
`Bootstrap` and page defaults.

**Technical:**

* `inst/www/mascot.css`, `inst/www/mascot-host.js`: renamed internal custom properties to
  `--_mascot-size`, `--_mascot-source-*`, `--_mascot-drag-*`, `--_mascot-menu-*`, `--_mascot-tooltip-*`,
  `--_mascot-panel-tail` and `--_mascot-notification-offset`; copied inherited public `--mascot-*` hooks
  from the source anchor to `--_mascot-source-*` when moving floating mascots to `document.body`.

## 2026-10-12 — Separate motion switches in `mascot_motion_settings()` (`bf2aed2`, #239, #267)

**In brief:** Replaced the single `animate` toggle with independent switches for `idle`, `mood_change`,
`gestures`, `swap`, `minimising`, `restoring`, `others` and per-panel `messages` (`bubble`, `tooltip`,
`menu`).

**Technical:**

* `inst/www/mascot-motion.js`: exported `mascot.motion.settings` and `mascot.motion.panels` (frozen);
  updated `pose()`, `moving()`, `preparePatch()`, `controller.update()` and `controller.gesture()` to
  check `state.idle`, `state.mood_change`, `state.gestures` and `state.swap` independently.
* `inst/www/mascot-host.js`, `inst/www/mascot.css`: added Web Animations (`Element.prototype.animate`)
  transitions for minimise and restore (240 `ms` transform and opacity using a temporary
  `.mascot-motion-copy` canvas clone) and panel exit fades (150 `ms` inert `DOM` clone), plus a
  development-mode `shiny:client-message` warning when a server gesture is skipped because
  `gestures = false`.

## 2026-10-12 — Automatic phone sizing and patch contract (`2bd43fa`, `c9ef831`, #259, #261, #264, #266)

**In brief:** Floating mascots cap their default size at 96 pixels on narrow screens (`<= 575.98px`) when
`small_screen = "auto"`.

**Technical:**

* `inst/www/mascot-host.js`, `inst/www/mascot.css`: supported `small_screen: "auto"` in `validateSize()`
  and the `.mascot[data-floating="true"][data-small-screen="auto"]` media query
  (`min(var(--_mascot-size-default, 160px), 96px)`).

## 2026-10-12 — Shared `.mascot-panel` backend, `click` actions, tooltips and gaze (`fd50085`, `0417e2d`, #233, #237, #241, #244, #248, #249, #250, #254, #257, #263)

**In brief:** Unified speech bubbles, pop-up menus and action tooltips under one visual panel system, added
single-action click buttons with `WCAG` 1.4.13 hover tooltips, and made the mascot's pupils look towards
open menus or bubbles.

**Technical:**

* `inst/www/mascot-host.js`: replaced `popup_menu` with `click` (`type: 'none' | 'action' | 'menu'`),
  wrapping the canvas in a single native `<button class="mascot-button">` when clickable, emitting
  `input$<id>_click` (monotonic counter, ignoring key-repeat and drag releases), and managing
  `.mascot-tooltip` with a 150 `ms` pointer-leave grace timer and shared `Escape` listener.
* `inst/www/mascot-host.js`: added `inkBox()` (alpha-channel bounding-box scan via `getImageData` when a
  menu or tooltip opens) and `placePanel()` (shared placement with opposite-side and `auto` fallback choices
  inside `clipBounds()`, plus `--_mascot-panel-tail` positioning).
* `inst/www/mascot-host.js`: added `gazeSide()`, `gazePose()` and `refreshGaze()` to set held `look` and
  `lookY` pose overrides towards the active menu's resolved `data-side` or active bubble, compensating for
  horizontal `flip`.

## 2026-10-10 — Floating drag (`snap` and `free`), minimised drag and directional menus (`42227c9`, `6ed258d`, `5edadb3`, #220, #222, #225, #229, #231, #232)

**In brief:** Visitors can drag floating mascots (or their minimised restore button) with pointer capture
to snap to the nearest corner or drop freely inside the window, and open pop-up menus on a chosen side
(`auto`, `top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right`) with one menu open at a time.

**Technical:**

* `inst/www/mascot-host.js`, `inst/www/mascot.css`: added `listenDrag()`, `drop()`, `cancelDrag()`,
  `clampPoint()` and `nearestCorner()` with a 4-pixel movement threshold (`dragThreshold`),
  `setPointerCapture`, capture-phase click suppression after drag, 200 `ms` snap animation, and
  `input$<id>_position` event reporting.
* `inst/www/mascot-host.js`: tracked open menus in a shared `openMenus` set so opening one closes any
  other, paused bubble timers while a menu is open or while minimised, and transferred focus safely before
  hiding controls.

## 2026-10-10 — Remove `simplify_when_small` (`18403f2`, #219, #221)

**In brief:** Removed the separate small-size face drawing so every size draws the full character.

**Technical:**

* `inst/www/mascot-draw.js`, `inst/www/mascot-motion.js`, `inst/www/mascot-host.js`: removed the `small`
  boolean option and small-size branch in `drawEyes()`, `drawMouth()`, `drawBlush()` and `character()`.

## 2026-10-07 to 2026-10-10 — Host life cycle, late-mount queue, themes, menus, motion, size and placement (`8c09d2a`, `c42dd66`, `bc06a44`, `69086f3`, `b396562`, `266e442`, `17bea5a`, `637039d`, `009334b`)

**In brief:** Built `mascot-host.js` and `mascot.css`: the `Shiny` input binding (`mascot.mascot`) and
static-page host, custom message queue (`mascot:update`), speech bubbles, pop-up menus, light and dark page
theming with follower-role shading and `WCAG` 3:1 contrast warnings, floating corner placement, and
responsive sizing.

**Technical:**

* `inst/www/mascot-host.js`: created `window.mascot.host` (`{ mount, unmount, receive, state }`),
  registering `MascotBinding` on `Shiny.inputBindings` and `mascot:update` custom messages; bounded the
  pre-mount queue (`queueLimit = 20`) and added a two-second development-mode namespace mismatch hint
  (`suggestNamespace`).
* `inst/www/mascot-host.js`: implemented `resolveTheme()`, `shadeColour()` (`HSL` lightness and saturation
  shifts from leader roles in `description.follows`), `colourContrast()` (`WCAG` relative luminance), and
  `pageMode()` watching `[data-bs-theme]` and `body.quarto-dark` / `quarto-light` (defaulting to light when
  no page signal is present).
* `inst/www/mascot-host.js`: implemented floating `DOM` placement (`portal()` to `document.body` with a
  `.mascot-source` placeholder span to preserve `Shiny` `unbindAll` tear-down and source container
  visibility and styles), `ResizeObserver` device-pixel-ratio canvas scaling, and
  `#shiny-notification-panel` offset tracking.

* `inst/www/mascot-host.js`: mount serials and retained per-field revision watermarks
  (`message.replay`, `message.fields`, `record.fields`) let the server replay state after remounts;
  `playedGestures` prevents replaying a previously handled gesture (`c42dd66`).

# mascot 0.0.2

## 2026-10-06 — Animated character swaps (`ea35c6f`, #147, #173)

**In brief:** Swapping from one character to another waves and fades the old character out over one second,
then fades the new character in while waving over one second, handling rapid mid-swap changes and reversals
smoothly.

**Technical:**

* `inst/www/mascot-motion.js`: added `mascot.motion.frame` (`sceneFrame(ch, state, n)`) and `SwapState`
  (`at`, `until`, `outFrames`, `inFrames`, `opacity`, `outgoing` snapshot with `wave` and `recovery`
  continuations), off-screen buffer blending (`layer` canvas in `drawFrame()`) so part-level alpha never
  leaks during fade-out and fade-in, `controller.current()`, and `options.onChange(snapshot)`.
* `inst/www/mascot.js`: added `validColour` and cached character validation in a `WeakMap`.

## 2026-10-06 — Frame-stepping motion engine and five-second player (`853b448`, #27, #145)

**In brief:** Added `mascot-motion.js` for mood transitions (wiggle or hop), deterministic seeded blinking
and breathing, one-off `nod` and `wave` gestures, `prefers-reduced-motion` support, and a canvas player
that automatically stops its `requestAnimationFrame` loop after five seconds (150 frames).

**Technical:**

* `inst/www/mascot-motion.js`: added `window.mascot.motion` (`{ pose, validate }`) and
  `window.mascot.mount(canvas, ch, options)` returning
  `{ seek, update, setMood, gesture, pause, play, destroy }`; implemented `LCG` hash blinking
  (`Math.imul((seed >>> 0) ^ i, 1664525) + 1013904223`), smooth breathing fade over the final third of the
  150-frame window, and atomic `preparePatch()` validation.

## 2026-10-03 — Data-driven character engine (`4ba964a`, `f642d19`, #52, #66, #137, #138)

**In brief:** Turned Tessa's hard-coded drawing code into a generic engine (`mascot.js` and
`mascot-draw.js`) that validates and draws any character from its `JSON` description
(`inst/characters/<id>.json`).

**Technical:**

* `inst/www/mascot.js`: added data-driven `readCharacter`, `validateCharacter` and `draw` under
  `window.mascot` (`fps = 30`). Colour validation and `WeakMap` validation caching follow in `ea35c6f`.
* `inst/www/mascot-draw.js`: added `window.mascot.drawing` (`svgPath` parser for absolute `M/L/Q/C/Z`
  commands, `hexPath`, `drawPart`, `resolvePose`, `guardPose`, `anchors` returning world coordinates and
  2x2 linear matrices, `accessories` slot validation, and `FACE_STYLE` overrides).

## 2026-10-03 — Initial port of Tessa's canvas drawing code (`df97139`, #9, #24, #136)

**In brief:** Brought Tessa's deterministic `2D` canvas drawing code over from the prototype site
(`tools/animate/engine.js`).

**Technical:**

* `inst/www/mascot.js`, `inst/www/mascot-draw.js`: initial classic-script `IIFE` setup under
  `window.mascot` drawing Tessa's hexagon body, eyes, mouths, brows, blush, sweat, sparkle, arms and feet
  at 30 `fps` without `Math.random()` or wall-clock reads.
